terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: The CC0 side reference strongly establishes profile anatomy, mane layering, scale direction and pedestal. The opposite side is inferred by bilateral symmetry; the exact rear tail transition is only partially visible.

reasoning: The current mascot-like spheres fail because the reference silhouette is a tall tapered fish column supporting an angular lion head, not a round animal body.
The head requires separate brow, muzzle, nose, upper jaw, lower jaw and cavity volumes; the mane is a nested plate system rather than radial spikes.
Overlapping scales, a pectoral fin, tail/wave transition and layered ceramic pedestal are repeated identity systems visible at catalogue distance.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A complex tier is required because the identity rests on continuous organic volumes, deep mouth negative space, layered mane plates and dense repeated scale relief that must hold across multiple angles.

details.description: Broad swept mane plates form a flattened crown crest behind the brow rather than radial spikes.
A projecting brow plane shades the small inset eye and angles down toward the muzzle.
The muzzle projects forward with a broad rounded nose and downturned upper-lip contour.
A deep open mouth separates upper and lower jaws and contains the water outlet in shadow.
A separate lower jaw and rounded chin project below the water stream and overlap the throat.
Long flattened mane locks sweep from cheek and jaw toward the shoulder in overlapping vertical layers.
details.affects: rear head silhouette and neck overlap

details.description: One tapered pectoral fin projects upward from the front shoulder of the fish body.
Dense overlapping scalloped scales descend in staggered rows around the tapered fish body.
The fish torso narrows steadily toward the pedestal with a slight forward belly curve.
Carved tail and foam ridges blend the lower fish body into the wave pedestal rather than ending as a vertical cylinder.
Several horizontal blue-white wave crests wrap the pedestal in offset layers above the dark plinth.
The white aggregate surface is satin-matte while the blue pedestal mosaic carries tighter low-roughness highlights.
details.scale: macro material split with micro variation

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At catalogue-card distance the model reads immediately as Singapore's Merlion: a lion head with open water-spouting jaw and layered mane attached to a tapered overlapping-scale fish body on a blue wave pedestal.
Front, side, rear three-quarter and top-oblique views retain real volume, connected anatomy and a legible mouth cavity; the head must not read as a bear, cat mascot, or sphere with spikes.

featureGroups.name: Lion-head to fish-body silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: The head is angular and forward-projecting, the neck/mane overhangs a narrower tapered fish column, and the body terminates in a wave/tail transition instead of a second animal torso.
failureModes: the model reads as a bear or cat mascot
head and body are equal spherical masses
the fish body has no taper or tail transition

featureGroups.name: Brow, muzzle, nose, open jaw and mouth cavity
qualityCriteria: Brow and cheek planes frame small inset eyes; a broad muzzle leads to a projecting upper jaw, separate lower jaw and deep dark mouth cavity aligned with the water emitter.
failureModes: the mouth is a painted dot or closed muzzle
nose and eyes are oversized black mascot features
the water jet exits below or through the chin

featureGroups.name: Layered crown, cheek and rear mane plates
qualityCriteria: Broad swept mane locks overlap from crown to shoulder with directional flow and attached roots; they are flattened sculptural plates, not evenly spaced cones or spikes.
failureModes: mane reads as a ring of spikes
plates float away from the head or intersect the muzzle
rear mane collapses into a smooth helmet

featureGroups.name: Overlapping fish scales, pectoral fin and tail transition
qualityCriteria: Scales overlap in staggered downward-facing rows around the body, a pectoral fin projects from the shoulder, and the lower body blends into a carved tail/wave base with no floating ring ornaments.
failureModes: the body is smooth or furry
the tail and wave base are absent

featureGroups.name: Layered ceramic wave pedestal and water stream
qualityCriteria: The pedestal has multiple horizontal blue mosaic wave crests and a dark plinth; a coherent tapered water curve leaves the mouth cavity and lands beyond the base without reading as a rigid blue pole.
failureModes: pedestal is a plain cyan cylinder
water is an opaque constant-radius rod
wave crests float or fail to wrap the base

brow, muzzle, nose, eye and mouth-cavity placement delta
mane plate count, direction, overlap and root attachment delta
scale row overlap, fin placement and lower-body taper delta
wave pedestal layering and water-jet origin/arc delta

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.

Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto: Neutral 5000 K key from camera-left at 1.1 intensity reveals the white sculptural planes without clipping them.
Cool fill at 0.22 preserves the deep mouth and mane grooves while maintaining readable cavity contrast.
Soft rear rim at 0.35 separates mane plates and scales; ACES Filmic exposure 0.95 with contact shadow under the pedestal.
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
